Build a category curve export bundle (preferred alias)

Source: R/api-reports.R
category_curves_report.Rd

Build a category curve export bundle (preferred alias)

Usage

category_curves_report(
  fit,
  theta_range = c(-6, 6),
  theta_points = 241,
  digits = 4,
  include_fixed = FALSE,
  fixed_max_rows = 400,
  newdata = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

theta_range

Theta/logit range for curve coordinates.

theta_points

Number of points on the theta grid.

digits

Rounding digits for numeric graph output.

include_fixed

If TRUE, include a legacy-compatible fixed-width text block.

fixed_max_rows

Maximum rows shown in fixed-width graph tables.

newdata

Optional data frame with every non-Person facet, one row per rating context, using fitted level labels and no Theta column. For native GPCM MML, evaluates the full fitted predictor, including one or two slope families. Theta is reserved for the ability grid. Unknown/missing levels are refused; unobserved combinations of known levels are allowed and labelled. NULL retains reference profiles.

Value

A named list with category-curve components. Class: mfrm_category_curves.

Details

Preferred high-level API for category-probability curve exports. model_context records the fitted step/slope owners. curve_profiles maps each CurveGroup to the owner levels, including separate-owner GPCM. By default, curves are conditional reference profiles with additive locations fixed at zero; see the retained CurveBasis and PredictorOffset columns. Explicit newdata enables full-context one- and two-family GPCM MML curves. This helper does not compute calibration SEs or confidence intervals. plot(out) and its selected curve views use base graphics. Automatic as_ggplot() conversion of this bundle is unavailable because curve families have distinct targets and scales; extract probabilities and retain its curve-family and group columns for custom figures. For fitted CCC graphics, plot(fit, type = "ccc") has a dedicated conversion; review its reference-profile settings before comparing curves. Returns tidy curve coordinates and summary metadata for quick plotting/report integration without calling low-level helpers directly. The expected-score table also carries the per-curve score variance and information function. For GPCM, the information column follows the Muraki/Samejima identity \(a^2 \mathrm{Var}(X \mid \theta)\); for RSM / PCM, this reduces to the usual score variance because discrimination is fixed at one. The category_information table decomposes that total into category-level contributions, \(a^2 P_k(\theta)(k - E[X \mid \theta])^2\), whose sum equals the reported information at the same theta value. The cumulative_probabilities table follows the FACETS / Winsteps graph convention of accumulating modeled probabilities across ordered categories (P(X <= k) by default, with P(X >= k) also returned for flipped curves). cumulative_boundaries reports approximate theta values where P(X <= k) = .5, with BoundaryStatus and CrossingCount to avoid over-interpreting boundaries outside the requested theta range or with multiple crossings.

Without newdata, these are reference-profile curves. Estimated step parameters and, for GPCM, each step-facet group's estimated slope are retained, while additive facet main effects and fitted interactions are fixed at zero. The CurveBasis and PredictorOffset columns, and the corresponding entries in settings, make that conditioning explicit. Thus the curves do not represent an arbitrary observed Person-by-facet cell.

Explicit rating contexts

With newdata, curve_profiles maps each curve to InputRow in the saved newdata. It retains the step owner/level, effective discrimination (the product for two families), additive PredictorOffset, and ObservedContext. The predictor is Theta + PredictorOffset; facet locations and interactions are retained. No Person posterior or population integration is involved. Category and expected scores retain the internal scoring scale; CategoryLabel and boundary label columns retain the original score labels. Plot series use these original labels without changing the scoring rule.

cumulative_boundaries solves P(X <= k) = .5, equivalently P(X >= k+1) = .5, directly within theta_range. It is independent of theta_points and retains full numerical precision irrespective of digits. Binary boundaries use the analytic adjacent intersection. Other boundaries use bracketed root finding on a stable difference of unnormalized lower and upper category masses, avoiding subtraction of rounded probabilities. The root tolerance is 1e-10 in native ability units: the mass difference must change sign within that distance on either side of the reported root. The probability residual must also be at most 1e-8. These are numerical checks, not statistical uncertainty bounds. Out-of-range roots remain NA with outside_theta_range; failed numerical checks remain NA with numerical_failure and a reason. AndrichThreshold is the centered step offset; AdjacentThreshold is the ability where the adjacent probabilities are equal, including the context offset. Neither is generally the cumulative ThurstonianThreshold. Positive discriminations order cumulative thresholds even when an intermediate category is never most probable; ordering alone does not establish category adequacy. SE, CI_Lower, and CI_Upper are NA and CIEligible is FALSE.

Finite calculations are retained even when the source fit needs review. fit_readiness, settings$source_converged and the summary/plot notes retain that distinction. Two-family values remain provisional. Unobserved contexts are predictions under the fitted model, not an identification guarantee. Save the complete result with saveRDS(); summary(), plot() and plot_data() replay it without fitting, diagnostics or covariance calculation.

Interpreting output

Use this report to inspect:

  • where each category has highest probability across theta

  • where cumulative category probabilities cross .5

  • whether adjacent categories cross in expected order

  • whether probability bands look compressed (often sparse categories)

Recommended read order:

  1. summary(out) for compact diagnostics.

  2. out$probabilities, out$expected_ogive, and out$category_information for custom graphics.

  3. plot(out) for a default visual check, or plot(out, type = "cumulative") to inspect cumulative probabilities. plot(out, type = "information") to inspect curve-level information. Use plot(out, type = "category_information") when category-level contributions are needed.

References

Category response curves follow Andrich's rating-scale formulation, Masters' partial-credit model, and Muraki's generalized partial-credit model. The Information column for GPCM uses Muraki's item-information result obtained from Samejima's general polytomous information formula.

  • Andrich, D. (1978). A rating formulation for ordered response categories. Psychometrika, 43(4), 561-573.

  • Masters, G. N. (1982). A Rasch model for partial credit scoring. Psychometrika, 47(2), 149-174.

  • Muraki, E. (1992). A generalized partial credit model: Application of an EM algorithm. Applied Psychological Measurement, 16(2), 159-176. doi:10.1177/014662169201600206

  • Muraki, E. (1993). Information functions of the generalized partial credit model. Applied Psychological Measurement, 17(4), 351-363. doi:10.1177/014662169301700403

Typical workflow

  1. Fit model with fit_mfrm().

  2. Run category_curves_report() with suitable theta_points.

  3. Use summary() and plot(); export tables for manuscripts/dashboard use. plot(out) gives a four-panel overview. Use preset = "monochrome" for grayscale/line-type output and boundary_status = "none" when cumulative .5 boundary lines should be suppressed. plot(out, type = "category_probability") and plot(out, type = "conditional_probability") are explicit aliases for the same category-probability curves as type = "ccc". The historical conditional alias is ordinary P(k), not the FACETS adjacent-conditional curve P(k)/(P(k-1)+P(k)); prefer the unambiguous "ccc" name. Use plot_data(out, component = "plot_long") when rebuilding the curves with ggplot2, plotly, or another R graphics system.

See also

category_structure_report(), rating_scale_table(), plot.mfrm_fit(), mfrmr_reports_and_tables, mfrmr_visual_diagnostics

Examples

toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score", method = "JML", maxit = 300)
out <- category_curves_report(fit, theta_points = 101)
summary(out)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Which cumulative boundaries apply to a specified rater and criterion?
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
gpcm_fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  model = "GPCM", method = "MML", step_facet = "Criterion",
  slope_facet = "Rater", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,
  category_policy = "preserve", quad_points = 61)
contexts <- unique(ratings[c("Rater", "Criterion")])[1:2, ]
curves <- category_curves_report(gpcm_fit, newdata = contexts)
curves$cumulative_boundaries[, c("CurveGroup", "UpperCategoryLabel",
  "ThurstonianThreshold", "AdjacentThreshold", "BoundaryStatus")]
summary(curves) # Inspect source readiness and interval limitations too.
plot(curves, type = "cumulative")
} # }
